contexts.text: A covenant... was (therefore) established by the laws of society given from the Lord in the Jewish Church, called testimonies...
That it may be a witness unto me () = certainty.
The Lord Himself was represented by the testimony in the ark.
For a testimony () = that they may know, and not make it a pretext that they have been ignorant.
Jegar-sahadutha means the heap of witness, in the idiom of Syria. Explained.

A witness = confirmation of good through truth, and of truth by good; and hence a testimony = the good from which is truth, and the truth which is from good. Illustrated. AC 4197:8, Illustrated. AC 4197:9, Explained.

Aaron laid it up before the testimony () = that it was in the Divine presence... The testimony = the Divine... because, in the universal sense, the testimony means the Word; and the Word is truth Divine, thus the Lord.

That the testimony = the Lord as to Divine truth, is evident from the ark in which was the Law... which is called the testimony. That the tabernacle derived all its sanctity from it; and that the testimony was the Holy Divine itself, is evident from...
The word of their testimony () = truth Divine received by man. AC 9503:2.
The testimony, or Law, in the ark, represented the Lord. AC 9482.
The reason the testimony, or Law, in the ark = the Lord, is that the testimony = Divine truth, (which) is the Lord in Heaven.
Thou shalt put the testimony to the ark () = the Divine truth, which is the Lord in Heaven. The ark = Heaven; and the testimony, the Divine truth, thus the Lord in Heaven. AC 9519. AC 9524.

A distinction is made in the Word between laws, statutes, judgments, precepts, testimonies, etc... as in the testimony of Jehovah is firm, making wise the simple... From these things it may be evident that testimony = the Divine truth, which bears witness concerning the Lord; thus the Word; for this, in the supreme sense, treats of the Lord alone, and then, in the internal sense, bears witness concerning Him, that is, teaches Him, and the truths of faith and goods of love which are from Him. Illustrated.

That the Divine truth which proceeds from the Lord is called the testimony from the fact that it testifies concerning the Lord. Illustrated... To this end came I into the world, that I may bear testimony to the Truth.
The testimony = the Lord as to Divine truth. AC 9785. AC 10304. AC 10375. AC 10451.
The testimony = the Lord. AE 283:14. AE 727:11.
The testimony of Jesus () = the Divine truth which is from Him and about Him.
The testimony = the Lord as to the Word.
The testimony is described first, by which is meant the Lord.
This Law is called a covenant because it conjoins; and a testimony because it bears witness...
False testimonies, etc. with the concupiscences to them, are the sins which are to be shunned. Explained.
In proportion as anyone shuns false testimonies of every kind as sins, he loves the Truth. General article. AE 949:3.
To bear witness falsely. Defined.

Who bore witness to the Word of God, and to the testimony of Jesus Christ () = who from the heart, and thus in light, receive Divine truth from the Word, and acknowledge the Human of the Lord to be Divine... The Angels bear witness, that is, see, acknowledge, and receive from the heart in light, and confess, the truths of the Word; especially this truth: that the Human of the Lord is Divine. AR 35. AE 10, Explained. AE 52.

As to the spiritual signification of bearing witness, it is predicated of the Truth, for the reason that in the world the Truth is to be borne witness to; and, when it has been borne witness to, it is acknowledged. But in Heaven the Truth itself bears witness concerning itself, because it is the very light of Heaven... And, as the Lord is the Truth itself... He is, in Heaven, the testimony of Himself. Hence it is evident what is meant by the testimony of Jesus Christ. Illustrated.
The souls of them that were slain... for the testimony which they held () = those hated and rejected by the evil on account of... their acknowledgement of the Lord's Divine Human. AE 392.
In Heaven, testimony is given solely to those who acknowledge the Lord's Divine Human; for the Lord is He who bears witness, and He gives to the Angels to bear witness.
That the Lord is the God of Heaven and earth, and that His Human is Divine, is the testimony. Illustrated.
And that the second essential of the New Church, which is conjunction with the Lord by a life according to the commandments, is also the testimony. Illustrated.

When they shall have finished their testimony () = after the Lord has taught that He is the God of Heaven and earth, and that there is conjunction with Him by a life according to the commandments. ( = at the end of the Church, when the Divine of the Lord is no longer acknowledged, and hence there is no longer good of love and truth of doctrine. AE 649.)

They overcame him... by the word of their testimony () = victory... through the acknowledgement that the Lord is the God of Heaven and earth, and that the precepts of the decalogue are precepts of life according to which men must live. ( = through the confession and acknowledgement of the Divine in His Human. AE 749). AE 329:20.
Testimony = the Divine Truth; in especial, these two things.

The remnant of her seed, who keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ () = novitiates, who receive the doctrine concerning the Lord, and concerning the decalogue. ( = who acknowledge the Divine in the Lord's Human. AE 770.)

The temple of the tabernacle of the testimony () = the inmost of Heaven, where is the Lord in His Holiness in the Word, and in the law which is the decalogue. ( = interior Divine truth in the Word revealed by the Lord. AE 948).
That the law which is the decalogue was called the testimony. Illustrated. AE 392:6.

I am of thy brethren who have the testimony of Jesus () = ... that he is in conjunction with the Lord, through the acknowledgement of the Divine in His Human, and a life according to His commandments. AE 1230.

For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy () = that the acknowledgement that the Lord is the God of Heaven and earth, together with a life according to His commandments, is, in the universal sense, the all of the Word and its derivative doctrine. Explained. AE 1232.
The souls of them that were beheaded for the testimony of Jesus () = those rejected... because they had worshipped the Lord, and had lived according to the truths of His Word. Explained.
The testimony of Jesus = confession from faith in Him.
This Law is called... the testimony, because it confirms the articles of the covenant; for... testimony, in the Word, = the confirmation and witnessing of the articles of (conjunction).
For to bear witness = to acknowledge at heart.
To bear witness. and testimony. Illustrated.
That testimony = confession of the Lord; and the Lord Himself. Illustrated. AE 392:7.
That testimony = the Lord; and, with man, the confession of the Lord from the heart; and in in special, the acknowledgement of the Divine of the Lord in His Human. Illustrated. AE 392:9, Illustrated.
Hence the Word before the Lord's advent is called the old Covenant; and that after His advent, the New Covenant; it is also called the Testament, Old and New; but it should be called the Testimony.
Testimony = that in the Word which teaches goods of life; law, that which teaches truths of doctrine. Illustrated.
False witness. Defined. (See TCR 321.)
The testimony of Jesus = the acknowledgement of the Divine of the Lord in His Human; and that He alone is to be worshipped and adored.
